title: Tokyo dark — Respect for the Aged Day, the first of three consecutive JPX holidays that bracket the US 2Y/5Y/7Y auction block
source: EST: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, the page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads verbatim 'Sep. 21 (Mon.) Respect for the Aged Day', 'Sep. 22 (Tue.) Holiday 2', 'Sep. 23 (Wed.) Autumnal Equinox', under the page's own standing rule 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' Corroborated at a second, independent primary in the same session: Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS), whose 2026 rows read 2026/9/21 敬老の日, 2026/9/22 休日, 2026/9/23 秋分の日. Statute backs the date: Respect for the Aged Day is fixed at the third Monday of September by Japan's Act on National Holidays, and September 2026's third Monday is the 21st. Stays estimate on the two standing counts the sibling jpx-market-closure entries already record, neither of them date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED during the treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22 adjacency sweep (2026-09-15, D-7). The corridor already tracked nine events on 09-17 and 09-18 and six on 09-23/09-24, but carried NO entry for the three-day Tokyo blackout sitting between them, even though the jpx-market-closure genre exists on this calendar (2026-11-23, 2026-12-31, 2027-03-22). Counting weekends, JPX is shut for FIVE consecutive sessions, Sat 2026-09-19 through Wed 2026-09-23 — the longest single blackout run in the 2026 calendar, and it covers the US 2-Year note auction (09-22) and the 5-Year (09-23) outright. WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN, measured rather than assumed by the proposing sweep: a Tokyo holiday does NOT depress the indirect-bidder share of a US coupon auction. Across 1,108 Treasury note/bond auctions since 2016 (Fiscal Data auctions_query, shares over competitive accepted, pulled direct 2026-09-15), the 37 that landed on a Japanese national holiday drew mean indirect 63.35% against 61.89% on Tokyo-open days — the WRONG SIGN for the hunch, Welch t=+0.850; dealer takedown 20.87% vs 23.52%, t=-1.412. On 2-Year notes alone (n=171) the null is nearly exact: dark 55.22% (n=9) vs open 55.44% (n=162), t=-0.050. Restricted to auctions inside a blackout of three or more consecutive dark sessions (n=15), mean indirect 60.57% vs 61.89%. Direct precedent: the 2025-09-23 2-Year auction was itself held on Autumnal Equinox Day and printed indirect 57.7% / dealer 11.5%, both on that series' own norm. So this entry exists to be ON THE RECORD as corridor context and to STOP a future session attributing a weak 09-22 or 09-23 indirect print to the blackout — not because a price channel is claimed. Impact low: this repo tracks no Japan-listed symbol and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or Tokyo-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
